At the parent (4cf7b1e), check-results therefore calls retry_urlopen against statsapi.mlb.com: game feed 778899, and if that game is final but the batter is missing, the 2026-04-01 schedule and each of its final games. But the red run's duration and outbound traffic depend on the host: up to about 60 s on a blackholed network (three 15 s timeouts plus 5 s and 10 s retry sleeps), and possibly a dozen feed fetches if the network is up. Without network, the streak check would even pass at the parent, because the error branch returns before update_streak. So the red run demonstrates the missing skip of an already-resolved date (the contract's second clause), not the double-count itself. The runner will accept it (a builtin AssertionError at the declared line), but whether a message-text check counts as the contract assertion is your call.
